Subject: Proposed DPA (MedSafe) — training clause question

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Attached is MedSafe's standard DPA (PDF) — our legal team marked a couple of key items we need to resolve before we can proceed to procurement and DocuSign. The main open item for us is the data-use paragraph that references "service improvement" / "model training."

Our position: MedSafe cannot allow use of Customer Data for model training or derivative model improvement unless the customer explicitly opts in at the account level. We typically allow aggregated, de-identified telemetry for reliability analytics, but not any form of training.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a prohibition on "training or model improvement" for Customer Data, with the alternative of a separate opt-in program (if the customer chooses)? If not, what narrow language would you accept (definitions, scope, and any technical controls)?

Also looping in our Privacy Officer Jeff Ramos on this thread.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
MedSafe Health

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending this over. I appreciate the clarity from MedSafe's side.

Quick note: I want to make sure we keep momentum toward DocuSign. I've looped in Marissa (our commercial counsel) and Karthik (privacy/infrastructure lead) to propose redlines that aim to be as narrow as possible while preserving Redwood's ability to operate and improve product quality. Our typical approach has been: define "Training" and "Customer Data" precisely, carve out telemetry/operational analytics, and add an explicit opt-in path for model improvement.

Would you be open to reviewing a short set of redlines that carve out non-training telemetry and limit any training use to (a) de-identified, aggregated datasets and (b) data for which the customer has provided explicit opt-in? If yes, we'll share a marked-up DPA by end of day tomorrow.

Subject: Redwood proposed redlines — definitions and technical limits

Hi Sarah — thanks for the thread. I reviewed MedSafe's proposed DPA and prepared a short set of commercial/legal redlines intended to be narrow and explicit. I'm attaching the redlined DOCX, but the key points are summarized below so they are easy to review:

1) Define terms
- "Customer Data": data provided to Redwood by or on behalf of MedSafe under the Agreement.
- "Training": the use of Customer Data to adjust, fine-tune, or otherwise change model weights, architecture, or parameters for the purpose of improving model performance.

2) Accepted uses (we propose):
- Operational analytics: Redwood may collect and use aggregated, de-identified operational telemetry (latency, error rates, anonymized token counts) for service reliability, capacity planning, and debugging.
- Quality monitoring: Redwood may run generated outputs against synthetic test prompts and internally-held non-customer datasets for quality assurance.

3) Prohibited uses unless explicit opt-in:
- Using Customer Data for Training as defined above unless MedSafe provides an explicit opt-in via contract addendum or account-level setting.

4) Subprocessors and transfers
- We'll provide our current subprocessor list and commit to 30 days' notice of changes for processors that could access Customer Data.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood will rely on SCCs and equivalent safeguards; we can add a clause requiring notice and additional controls for transfers outside the EEA or US (as relevant).

5) Technical controls we can offer
- Option to enable strict KV cache isolation and request-scoped tokenization to reduce retention of raw inputs;
- Retention window guarantees for Customer Data used for debugging (e.g., 30 days default, configurable).

If this high-level approach is acceptable, the attached redline inserts explicit language in Sections 2.1, 7.3, and 9.2 (definitions, data-use, subprocessors). We're trying to be pragmatic: preserve a clear prohibition on training without blocking necessary operational analytics.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3_marissa_redlines.docx

Subject: Re: Redwood proposed redlines — definitions and technical limits

Marissa — thanks for the thorough breakdown and for keeping the redlines narrow. A few follow-ups from our side: 

- Procurement wants the prohibition on "Training" to be unequivocal for MedSafe Customer Data unless MedSafe opts in. "Operational analytics" as you describe is likely acceptable, but we want an explicit exclusion of any use for "model parameter updates" or "fine-tuning."

- Our Privacy Officer (Jeffrey) asked whether Redwood can provide a short tech note on how KV cache isolation and retention windows work in practice (we'd like to include that as evidence for our internal privacy review).

- On subprocessors: we require either (a) a fixed approved list in the DPA or (b) notice + right to object for material changes. Can Redwood offer a 30-day notice plus a right-to-object for changes that would cause data to be processed in an additional country or by a new class of cloud provider?

Procurement is prepared to sign once we have (1) final language with a clear training prohibition unless opt-in, (2) a short tech note, and (3) the DocuSign package. I'll share our counter-redlines (attached) so you can confirm parity.

Sarah
Sarah Lin
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
MedSafe Health

Subject: Final — agreed DPA text and DocuSign package

Hi team — great progress this week. Per our legal discussion, we agreed on the following commercial outcome:

• Training prohibition: Redwood will not use MedSafe Customer Data for "Training" (as defined in the attached executed DPA) unless MedSafe provides explicit written opt-in.
• Operational telemetry: Redwood may collect aggregated, de-identified telemetry for reliability and capacity planning (explicitly excluded from "Training").
• Subprocessors: Redwood will provide current subprocessor list and give 30 days' notice for material changes; MedSafe has a right to object to new subprocessors that would cause cross-border movement to a jurisdiction not previously listed.
• Technical note: Karthik attached a short tech note describing KV cache isolation and configurable retention windows for customer inputs; this will be included in the procurement package.

Next steps:
1) DocuSign execution: please sign the DocuSign package here — https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=12345&v=1&formid=MSF-DPA-8392
2) Procurement will confirm once DocuSign is complete and then we'll hand off to onboarding for connector/region planning.

Attachments included in the envelope: Redwood_DPA_v3_marissa_redlines.docx (finalized), Tech_Note_KV_cache_ISO.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to getting MedSafe live.
